cues: Your child gets straight A's. So why do they fall apart at the first setback?
The book Thrivers, by psychologist Michele Borba, explains why.

data.line2: but falls apart at the first setback?

cues: Strivers chase grades and approval, and they're terrified of failure.
Thrivers are driven from within. They see failure as a lesson, and bounce back.
The difference? Seven character strengths, and every one can be taught.
Self-confidence. Empathy. Self-control. Integrity. Curiosity. Perseverance. And optimism.
Empathy plus curiosity equals deeper relationships.
Put the phone away. Ask how they really feel. And let them solve their own problems.

tips: Let them solve their own problems
